```{r}
#| echo: false
source("covid-time-series-NZ-2.R")
```

## The big picture

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-pos: slide
stages = data.frame(
  x = as.Date(c("2020-04-08", "2021-01-31", "2021-08-31", "2022-01-01")),
  y = c(1500, 2600, 7000, 75000),
  label = c("Lockdown", "Elimination", "Delta", "The end...")
)
labels <- geom_label(data = stages, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label), alpha = 0.5, lw = 0, vjust = 0)
(g1 + labels) / g1d
```

##

* Daily hand-entered data from government website 
* (My) first serious exploration of the _R_ `tidyverse` and the `ggplot` visualization library
* Confirmed a decision to transition 'advanced GIS' to 'intro spatial data science'
* Biggest challenge was data buried in proprietary systems

## Epidemiology $\neq$ geography {data-background="images/snow-map.jpg" data-background-opacity="50%"}
### Implicitly it _is_
### In practice, it _is not_
### Populations understood as _aggregate_
### Not _distributed_ and _variegated_

image source [commons.wikimedia.org](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Snow-cholera-map-1.jpg) from Snow, John. 1855. _On the Mode of Communication of Cholera_, 2nd Ed, John Churchill, New Burlington Street, London, England.

## Branching process model

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column style="font-size:60%;line-height:1em;"}

![](images/contact-process-model-plank-et-al.png)

Plank MJ at al. 2020. [A stochastic model for COVID-19 spread and the effects of Alert Level 4 in Aotearoa New Zealand](https://dx.doi.org/10.1101/2020.04.08.20058743). Preprint on medrxiv.org. doi: 10.1101/2020.04.08.20058743.

:::

::: {.column}

Each infection has a time-varying probability of causing future infections

[New infections may _not_ occur depending on local $R_0$ at time they are scheduled]{.fragment}

[May occur non-locally in another connected locale]{.fragment}

:::

::::
